examName: Implementing Data Engineering Solutions Using Azure Databricks
note: Domains and weights follow Microsoft's published skills-measured outline for DP-750, 'Skills measured as of March 11, 2026'. Always check learn.microsoft.com for the current official breakdown before your exam, as Microsoft periodically revises exam blueprints.

domains.name: Set up and configure an Azure Databricks environment
subtopics: Choose an appropriate compute type, including job, serverless, warehouse, classic, and shared compute
Configure compute performance settings including node count, autoscaling, termination, node type, and pooling
Configure Photon acceleration, runtime and Spark version, and machine learning settings
Install libraries for a compute resource and configure access permissions to it
Apply naming conventions for isolation, development environment, and external sharing
Create catalogs, schemas, and volumes based on requirements
Create tables, views, and materialised views
Implement a foreign catalog by configuring connections
Implement DDL operations on managed and external tables
Configure AI/BI Genie instructions for data discovery

domains.name: Secure and govern Unity Catalog objects
subtopics: Grant privileges to users, service principals, and groups for securable objects
Implement table-, column-, and row-level access control
Access Azure Key Vault secrets from within Azure Databricks
Authenticate data access with service principals and resource access with managed identities
Create and preserve table and column definitions and descriptions for discovery
Configure attribute-based access control using tags and policies
Configure row filters and column masks
Apply data retention policies
Set up data lineage tracking with Catalog Explorer, including owner, history, and dependencies
Configure audit logging and design a secure strategy for Delta Sharing

domains.name: Prepare and process data
subtopics: Design ingestion logic and choose an ingestion tool, including Lakeflow Connect, notebooks, and Data Factory
Choose a loading method and a table format, including Delta, Parquet, and Iceberg
Design a partitioning scheme and choose a slowly changing dimension type
Design temporal history tables and a clustering strategy including liquid clustering and Z-ordering
Choose between managed and unmanaged tables
Ingest data with Lakeflow Connect, notebooks, SQL methods, CDC feeds, and Spark Structured Streaming
Ingest streaming data from Azure Event Hubs and with Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines and Auto Loader
Profile data, resolve duplicate, missing, and null values, and choose column data types
Transform data by filtering, grouping, joining, denormalising, pivoting, and unpivoting
Implement validation checks, schema enforcement, schema drift handling, and pipeline expectations

domains.name: Deploy and maintain data pipelines and workloads
subtopics: Design order of operations and choose between notebooks and Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines
Design task logic for Lakeflow Jobs and implement error handling in pipelines and notebooks
Create jobs with triggers, schedules, alerts, and automatic restarts
Apply version control best practices with Git, including branching, pull requests, and conflict resolution
Implement a testing strategy including unit, integration, end-to-end, and user acceptance tests
Configure and package Databricks Asset Bundles and deploy them by CLI and REST API
Monitor and manage cluster consumption to optimise performance and cost
Troubleshoot and repair Lakeflow Jobs, Spark jobs, and notebooks
Investigate caching, skew, spill, and shuffle issues using the DAG, the Spark UI, and query profile
Optimise Delta tables with OPTIMIZE and VACUUM, and configure log streaming and alerts in Azure Monitor
